The formula for the area of the triangle is \[ \mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}bc\sin{A}, \] where $\angle{A}$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$

Here, we have

\begin{align} с & = AB = 36,\\ b & = AC = 36,\\ m \angle{A} & = 70^\circ. \end{align}

Since \[ \sin{70^{\circ}} = 0.939\,693, \] rounded to six decimal places, we calculate the area as follows: \begin{align*} \mathcal{A} &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 36 \cdot 36 \cdot \sin{70^\circ} \\[5pt] &=648 \cdot (0.939\,693) \\[5pt] & \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{609\,\text{mi}^2}, \end{align*} rounded to the nearest integer.

example.title: Calculating the Area of a Triangle

question.text: Find the area of $\triangle ABC.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The formula for the area of the triangle is \[ \mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin{C}, \] where $\angle{C}$ is between the sides of lengths $a$ and $b.$

Here, we have

\begin{align} b & = CA = 8,\\ a & = CB = 10,\\ m \angle{A} & = 43^\circ. \end{align}

Since \[ \sin{43^{\circ}} = 0.681\,998, \] rounded to six decimal places, we calculate the area as follows: \begin{align*} \mathcal{A} &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 8 \cdot \sin{43^\circ} \\[5pt] &= 40 \cdot (0.681\,998) \\[5pt] & \approx 27.28\,\text{cm}^2, \end{align*} rounded to two decimal places.

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating an Angle or Side of a Triangle Given the Area of a Triangle

question.text: The area of ​​the triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $15 \text{ cm}^2.$ Find $m \angle A.$
question.explanation:
The formula for the area of the triangle is \[ \mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}bc\sin{A}, \] where $\angle{A}$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$

Here \begin{align} c & = AB = 5 \,\text{ cm},\\ b & = AC=12 \,\text{cm}\\ \end{align} Therefore, we can calculate $m\angle A$ as follows: \begin{align} \mathcal{A} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot c \cdot \sin A \\[5pt] 15 & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 12 \cdot 5 \cdot\sin A\\[5pt] 15 & =30 \cdot \sin A\\[5pt] \dfrac{15}{30} & = \sin A \\[5pt] \sin A & =\dfrac{1}{2} \\[5pt] m\angle A & = 30^\circ. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating an Angle or Side of a Triangle Given the Area of a Triangle

question.text: The area of ​​the triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $\dfrac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} \text{ cm}^2.$ Find $AC.$
question.explanation:
The formula for the area of the triangle is \[ \mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}bc\sin{A}, \] where $\angle{A}$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$

Here \begin{align} c & = AB = 6 \text{ cm},\\ b & = AC,\\ m \angle A & = 45^\circ. \end{align}

Since \[ \sin{45^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \] we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows: \begin{align} \mathcal{A} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot c \cdot \sin A \\[5pt] \dfrac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot 6 \cdot \sin{45^\circ} \\[5pt] \dfrac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot 6 \cdot \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right) \\[5pt] \dfrac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & = \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}\,b}{2} \\[5pt] \dfrac{21\cancel{\sqrt{2}}}{\cancel{2}} & = \dfrac{3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}\,b}{\cancel{2}} \\[5pt] 3b & = 21\\[5pt] b & = 7\text{ cm}. \end{align}

We conclude that $AC = 7\,\textrm{cm}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.text: Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the parallelogram $ABCD?$
question.explanation:
The diagonal $\overline{BD}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $\triangle ABD$ (see the illustration).

Computing the area of $\triangle ABD,$ we find \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{ABD} &= \dfrac 1 2 (10) (6) \sin 38^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 30 \cdot \sin 38^\circ \\[5pt] &\approx 18.470, \end{align*} rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

\begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} &= 2\mathcal{A}_{ABD} \\[0pt] &= 2 \cdot 18.470 \\[0pt] &= 36.940. \end{align*}

So, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram is $37.$

example.title: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.text: Find, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD.$
question.explanation:
The diagonal $\overline{BD}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $\triangle CBD$ (see the illustration below).

Computing the area of $\triangle CBD,$ we find \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{CBD} &= \dfrac 1 2 (21) (12) \sin 66^ \circ \\[3pt] &= 126 \cdot \sin 66^\circ \\[0pt] &\approx 115.107, \end{align*}

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

\begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} &= 2\mathcal{A}_{CBD} \\[0pt] &= 2 \cdot 115.107\\[0pt] &= 230.214. \end{align*}

Thus, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram is $230.$

example.title: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle Given the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.text: The area of $ABCD$ is $175 \text{ in}^2.$ What is the area of $\triangle BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?
question.explanation:
Let's start by finding the area of $\triangle ABD.$ We get

\begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot AB \cdot AD \cdot \sin{A}\\[5pt] &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 27 \cdot 30 \cdot \sin 35^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 405 \cdot \sin 35^\circ \\[5pt] & = 232.298 \ldots\\[5pt] & \approx 232 \textrm{ in}^2, \end{align*} rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of $\triangle ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $\triangle BCD.$ Therefore, \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle BCD} & = \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} - \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} \\[3pt] & = 232 - 175 \\[3pt] & = 57\, \textrm{ in}^2. \end{align*}

question.text: The area of $ABCD$ is $112 \,\text{cm}^2.$ Rounded to the nearest integer, the area of $\triangle BCD = $
question.explanation:
Let's start by finding the area of $\triangle ABD.$ We get

\begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} & =\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot AB \cdot AD \cdot \sin{A}\\[5pt] &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 24 \cdot 16 \cdot \sin 55^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 192 \cdot \sin 55^\circ \\[5pt] & = 157.277 \ldots\\[5pt] & \approx 157\, \textrm{ cm}^2 \end{align*} rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of $\triangle ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $\triangle BCD.$ Therefore, \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle BCD} & = \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} - \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} \\[2pt] & = 157 - 112 \\[2pt] & = 45 \,\textrm{ cm}^2. \end{align*}
